title: Announcing MCP support in Apigee hybrid: agentic tools that run in your own cluster
key_facts: Apigee is Google Cloud's API management product; MCP support was first previewed in Apigee last December.
With Apigee hybrid 1.17.0, released 14 Sep 2026, Model Context Protocol (MCP) support is available and the MCP data plane runs inside the customer's own Kubernetes cluster.
Each operation in an OpenAPI 3.0.x spec becomes an MCP tool through an MCP Discovery Proxy, with no MCP server code to write.
MCP request traffic stays inside the cluster; configuration is pulled by a sidecar, so Google never opens a connection into the customer network.
MCP is optional and off by default; it is enabled with a Helm setting (enableMcpServer: true), and enabling or disabling triggers a staged canary release of runtime pods.
Defaults are two MCP replicas, autoscaling to ten.
Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry can follow a call from the AI client through Apigee to the backend.

MCP request traffic stays inside your cluster.
why_it_matters_hint: Companies that must keep systems in their own data centres can let AI agents call their APIs without sending that traffic to Google.
notes: Vendor's own blog; first public announcement appears to be this post, while the software release itself is dated 14 Sep 2026.
